subject: EastUS3: Staged KV-cache preservation & rolling restarts (maintenance advisory)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.ai, jordan.reyes@acme.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: EastUS3: Staged KV-cache preservation & rolling restarts (maintenance advisory)

Hello Jordan / Acme Ops team,

We’re planning a brief, staged maintenance operation in EastUS3 on Sunday 2027-05-30 between 02:00 and 05:00 UTC. The primary objective is a kernel/driver compatibility handoff that will be executed as a rolling restart across small host cohorts. This notice is to: (1) explain our steps to preserve model KV caches (to avoid cold-start regressions), (2) detail the expected customer impact, and (3) outline rollback & postmortem plans.

Key points:
- Window: 2027-05-30 02:00–05:00 UTC. We will operate in 20–30 minute cohorts to limit blast radius.
- Impact: We expect transient latency increases for affected hosts during each cohort (3–7s spike for the first few requests). No request loss is expected; however, clients could observe short-lived cold-cache behavior for in-flight models unless sessions are pinned.
- KV cache preservation: We will use a warmed checkpoint/replica rolling sequence to attempt in-place KV reuse where possible. When KV reuse isn’t possible, we’ll prioritize graceful draining and immediate traffic migration to healthy hosts to reduce tail latency.
- Fallback: If we detect error rates >0.5% or sustained latency beyond 10s for more than 5 minutes, we will pause the rollout and fallback to the previous driver image for the remainder of the region.
- Support: On-call SREs will be available in the maintenance channel and via pager.

Requested action from Acme:
1) If you have long-lived sessions pinned to specific host groups, consider enabling session affinity relaxation between 30 minutes before and 60 minutes after the window so we can migrate traffic without session drops.
2) Share any critical model names you prefer we avoid moving during the window (reply to this thread).

Attachments: maintenance-runbook.pdf (overview + rollback checklist).

We’ll post a short postmortem within 48 hours and share the full incident timeline in OPS-9581. Please reach out if you have questions or if the window conflicts with your major batch jobs.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Program Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: maintenance-runbook.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

----

From: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EastUS3: Staged KV-cache preservation & rolling restarts (maintenance advisory)

Thanks for the heads up, Stephanie. A couple quick clarifications from our side:  
- Our traffic pattern for production models M-100 / M-annotator includes many short requests but relies on persistent KV state for optimization. If hosts are restarted we’ll see a big cold-start penalty for several minutes.  
- Can you confirm whether the warm checkpoint approach will migrate KV for in-flight model versions or only for pre-warmed replicas? If it’s only pre-warmed replicas we’d like to request that you avoid cohorts that include the host pool serving M-100 between 02:20–03:20 UTC (we have a deploy at 03:00 that day).

We can relax session affinity as requested but would appreciate confirmation on the exact cohorts to expect.

Jordan Reyes
SRE, Acme AI
[Quoted text follows]
> On Fri, 29 May 2027 at 08:23 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> > We’re planning a brief, staged maintenance operation in EastUS3 on Sunday 2027-05-30 between 02:00 and 05:00 UTC.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EastUS3: Staged KV-cache preservation & rolling restarts (maintenance advisory)

Hi Jordan, thanks — good questions. Short answers:  
- Warm checkpoint migration: we’ll only be able to carry KV forward automatically for model replicas that were proactively re-pinned into the warm-prep cohort (this is why we’re asking for session-affinity relaxation). For in-flight versions not pre-warmed, we cannot reliably transfer KV state; the host will evict and that model instance will experience a cold cache.
- Cohort scheduling: we plan cohorts at approximately 15–30 minute intervals. We will not touch the smaller M-100 host pool between 02:20–03:20 UTC per your request; that cohort is marked as "avoid" in the runbook.
- Recommended mitigation: enable a short client-side retry/backoff for 1 minute and spread traffic across replicas. If you want, our SREs can do a test-run on a staging subset earlier Saturday to validate warm migration.

I’ve attached the KV checklist with the precise steps we’ll run pre- and post-cohort.

Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Inference Serving
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: kv-cache-preservation-checklist.md]

----

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reyes <jordan.reyes@acme.ai>, ops@acme.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EastUS3: Staged KV-cache preservation & rolling restarts (maintenance advisory)

Jordan — confirmed. We’ve updated the runbook: cohort that would have included the M-100 pool is excluded and flagged for a separate, later window if needed. We’ll also run a staging validation on Saturday at 19:00 UTC with your team (opt-in) to exercise the warm checkpoint step.

Post-maintenance follow-up: we will publish a short postmortem within 48 hours and include the exact timing per cohort, any KV reuse rates we observed, and the timeline for any fallback activity. The postmortem will use the OPS-9581 ticket and the postmortem-template.docx attached for internal format.

If anything changes in the window we’ll notify you immediately. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Program Manager, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: postmortem-template.docx]
